affected_system: affordable housing production, preservation, subsidy, and compliance system
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of affordable-housing subsidy and delivery capacity
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for affordable-housing subsidy and delivery capacity
pair affordability-duration, need, leverage, and equity allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Units, affordability restrictions, occupancy, financing, condition, pipeline, and parcel feasibility are reconciled.
Modeled development feasibility is not treated as entitlement, financing close, or completed housing.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for affordable-housing subsidy and delivery capacity.

constraints.description: The affordable housing siting and preservation allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: housing development commissioner and affordable-housing finance director
decision_question: How should tax credits, loans, grants, vouchers, and technical capacity be allocated?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The affordable housing siting and preservation allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for affordable-housing subsidy and delivery capacity passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: affordability-duration, need, leverage, and equity allocation
independence_key.primary_outcome: eligible affordable home-years without assigned subsidy

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting affordable-housing subsidy and delivery capacity, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: eligible affordable home-years without assigned subsidy
distributional gap in eligible affordable home-years without assigned subsidy
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report a modeled subsidy allocation as an award, closing, or completed home.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for affordable-housing subsidy and delivery capacity passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate housing subsidy and preservation capacity
transportability_risks: Land law, subsidy programs, construction costs, finance, tenant protections, and markets differ.
Observed transactions may omit informal displacement and off-market preservation risks.
